=== EDIT: 0 What Pragmatism Means.md ===
--- AFTER ---
Whenever a dispute is serious, we ought to be able to show some practical difference that must follow from one side or the other's being right.[^6]
--- PARAGRAPH ---
The corpus of {}a ferocious metaphysical dispute{} was a squirrel--a live squirrel supposed to be clinging to one side of a tree-trunk; while over against the tree's opposite side a human being was imagined to stand. This human witness tries to get sight of the squirrel by moving rapidly round the tree, but no matter how fast he goes, the squirrel moves as fast in the opposite direction, and always keeps the tree between himself and the man, so that never a glimpse of him is caught. The resultant metaphysical problem now is this: DOES THE MAN GO ROUND THE SQUIRREL OR NOT? Which party is right{} depends on what you PRACTICALLY MEAN by 'going round' the squirrel. If you mean passing from the north of him to the east, then to the south, then to the west, and then to the north of him again, obviously the man does go round him, for he occupies these successive positions. But if on the contrary you mean being first in front of him, then on the right of him, then behind him, then on his left, and finally in front again, it is quite as obvious that the man fails to go round him, for by the compensating movements the squirrel makes, he keeps his belly turned towards the man all the time, and his back turned away. Make the distinction, and there is no occasion for any farther dispute. You are both right and both wrong according as you conceive the verb 'to go round' in one practical fashion or the other.
=== REPORT ===
Loss 0.1: I added eight statements as a new paragraph at the end of "0 What Pragmatism Means". They are the dispute setup ("The corpus of…", "This human witness…", "The resultant metaphysical problem…"), then "Which party is right… 'going round' the squirrel.", the two senses ("If you mean passing from the north…", "But if on the contrary you mean…"), then "Make the distinction…" and "You are both right and both wrong…". The repairs were as follows. "the dispute" in "The corpus of the dispute" was given a name span, "a ferocious metaphysical dispute", taken from the segment's first sentence. "I said," in "Which party is right" was handled with a first-person cut. I kept the whole antecedents for "the squirrel", "the man", "This human witness" and "The resultant metaphysical problem": these are the corpus, witness and problem sentences. I also kept the whole antecedent for "the distinction": the two sense sentences that state the two practical meanings of "going round". I judged "you" in "what you PRACTICALLY MEAN", "If you mean", "You are both right" and "you conceive" as addressed to anyone weighing the dispute, so generic, and left it unrepaired. I also left "Which party" unrepaired, since its referent is the parties to the dispute, which the earlier statements supply.
